papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There are no reliable risk models for predicting long-term survival after esophagectomy for esophageal cancer. We aimed to address this gap by developing and validating an all-cause mortality risk model to predict long-term survival probabilities in esophagectomy patients. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing esophagectomy for esophageal cancer in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (2012-2023; 280 hospitals) were studied. Vital status was determined by linkage to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Death Index and/or Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services inpatient data. Risk model to estimate survival probability was developed using stratified multivariable Cox regression. Discrimination was assessed using bootstrap-adjusted concordance index and time-dependent ROC. Calibration was evaluated by comparing observed to predicted survival probabilities. Generalizability was evaluated by internal-external repeated cross-validation. RESULTS: 16,056 esophageal cancer patients were included. Median follow-up was 5.4 years, with mean age of 65.7 years (SD=9.2). Five-year survival for pathologic stages I-IV were 62.0%, 45.9%, 31.1% and 23.7%, respectively. Most patients (76.8%) received neoadjuvant therapy with 19.0% pathological complete response (pCR) overall. Patients with pCR demonstrated higher 5-year overall survival (61.8% vs 40.6%). Bootstrap adjusted C-index was 0.68 (95%CI=0.67-0.68); incorporating postoperative complications into the model increased C-index to 0.70. CONCLUSIONS: A 10-year risk prediction model for all-cause mortality was developed using national-scale, real-world clinical data linked to long-term vital status data. This model showed excellent performance with accurate prediction of observed survival patterns in all patients, across all risk score groups, and for all pathologic stages and neoadjuvant treatment.

papers.authors: Cheon S, Kim KR, Lee H, Kim SH, Chung JE

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have led to a fundamental shift in lung cancer treatment, evidence regarding infections remains limited. Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is a rare but life-threatening opportunistic infection with high mortality if undiagnosed or untreated, making its risk assessment clinically critical. This study aimed to provide population-based comparative evidence on the risk of PJP between ICI therapy and conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy (CC) in patients with lung cancer. METHODS: Using the Korean nationwide claims data, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients newly diagnosed with lung cancer who initiated CC or ICI therapy between 2017 and 2022. After propensity score matching, incidence rate ratios (IRRs), Cox hazard ratios (HRs), and Fine-Gray subdistribution HRs (sHRs) were estimated. Sensitivity analyses were performed across clinically relevant subgroups, including those defined by advanced stage, surgical resection, radiotherapy, treatment line, ICI monotherapy, and systemic corticosteroid use. Additionally, risk patterns across specific ICI agents, including atezolizumab, pembrolizumab, durvalumab, and nivolumab, were evaluated in an exploratory analysis. RESULTS: After matching, 13,426 patients were included in each group. During follow-up, 27 and 66 PJP events occurred in the CC and ICI groups, respectively, corresponding to IRs of 3.35 and 7.77 per 1,000 person-years. ICI therapy was associated with a significantly higher risk of PJP (adjusted IRR 2.26, 95% CI 1.46-3.59; adjusted HR 2.83, 95% CI 1.81-4.44; adjusted sHR 2.63, 95% CI 1.68-4.12). In the exploratory analysis, significantly elevated IRRs, HRs, and sHRs were observed for durvalumab, pembrolizumab, and atezolizumab, while no clear association was observed for nivolumab because of the limited number of events. This association remained robust and consistent across various clinical contexts including cohorts defined by disease stage, treatment line, the use of monotherapy, and patients without systemic steroid exposure. CONCLUSIONS: ICI therapy is associated with a significantly increased risk of PJP compared with CC in patients with lung cancer. Given the potential severity of PJP, enhanced clinical vigilance is warranted during ICI treatment.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive cancer that shows limited response to immunotherapy. The mechanisms underlying immune evasion in ESCC remain unclear. This study aims to identify key regulators of immune exclusion in ESCC and assess their potential as therapeutic targets to enhance treatment efficacy. Methods: Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses were conducted to identify genes associated with immune exclusion in ESCC. Immunohistochemistry was used to validate protein expression in ESCC and adjacent normal tissues. Functional experiments, including pharmacologic inhibition and mouse xenograft models, were employed to investigate the roles of neutrophils and the protein kinase N2 (PKN2)-forkhead box C1 (FOXC1)-C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (CXCL8) pathway in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment. Neutrophil extracellular trap formation was assessed using immunofluorescence, electron microscopy, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Correlation and survival analyses were performed to link molecular findings with clinical outcomes. Results: Integrative analysis of single-cell transcriptomic data identified PKN2 as a critical contributor to immune exclusion in ESCC. Comparison of immune-reactive and nonreactive tumor groups revealed markedly elevated PKN2 expression in immune-excluded tumors. Mechanistically, PKN2 phosphorylates FOXC1 at threonine 232, preventing its interaction with the E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing 29 and inhibiting its proteasomal degradation. This results in FOXC1 stabilization, leading to a subsequent increase in CXCL8 secretion, a key neutrophil chemoattractant. The PKN2-FOXC1-CXCL8 signaling cascade recruits neutrophils, promoting neutrophil extracellular trap formation and contributing to immune exclusion. Furthermore, targeting the PKN2 pathway restored CD8+ T cell infiltration (P < 0.001) and synergistically enhanced anti-programmed cell death protein 1 efficacy, leading to a significantly lower tumor burden compared to monotherapy (P < 0.001). Conclusions: PKN2 critically mediates immune suppression in ESCC through the FOXC1-CXCL8-neutrophil regulatory network. Targeting this pathway may provide an effective strategy to overcome immune exclusion, enhance T cell infiltration, and improve the efficacy of immunotherapy in ESCC.

papers.authors: Garry JD, Chacon-Barahona J, Chung SJ, Frantz R, Rischard F, Hassoun P, Mathai S, Simpson C et al.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) associates with disease severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, prior studies focused on Group 1 disease; it is unknown whether DHEA-S associates with PH severity in other etiologies. It also remains unclear if DHEA-S associations with PH severity differ by sex or menopausal status. RESEARCH QUESTION: Do associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity differ by PH etiology, sex, or menopausal status? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We analyzed data from PVDOMICS, including 85 healthy controls and 710 participants with PH. Venous plasma DHEA-S levels were measured by ultraperformance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between DHEA-S levels and invasive hemodynamics, right ventricular (RV) systolic function, and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Analyses were stratified by sex and WSPH group, with exploratory stratification by menopausal status among subjects with Group 1 PH. RESULTS: DHEA-S levels were lower in all WSPH Groups compared with controls (adjusted p<0.01 for all). Associations between DHEA-S levels and PH severity metrics appeared most prominent in females with Group 1 PH. A doubling of DHEA-S was associated with a 2.8 mmHg (95% CI 1.6-4.1) lower mean pulmonary artery pressure, 3.2% (95% CI 2.0-4.4%) higher RV ejection fraction, and 22m (95% CI 11-33) farther 6MWD (all p<0.01). Higher DHEA-S associated with better RV function, but not pulmonary hemodynamics or 6MWD in females with Group 2 PH and males with Group 3 PH. In Group 1 PH, associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity appeared stronger in post-menopausal compared with premenopausal females. INTERPRETATION: Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Peripheral pulmonary lesions are increasingly detected through widespread computed tomography use, incidental imaging, and low-dose CT lung cancer screening programs. Diagnostic techniques have advanced substantially, including radial endobronchial ultrasound, virtual and electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy, ultrathin bronchoscopy, cryobiopsy, cone-beam CT (CBCT), augmented fluoroscopy, and robotic-assisted bronchoscopy. Despite this rapid technological evolution, the interpretation of benign or nonmalignant biopsy results remains one of the most consequential and underappreciated clinical challenges in pulmonary medicine. SUMMARY: A benign biopsy result from a peripheral pulmonary lesion must not be interpreted as a single, unambiguous entity. Specific benign diagnoses, nonspecific benign findings, atypia, suspicious results, and nondiagnostic samples each carry a distinct residual probability of malignancy and different implications for subsequent management. Recent consensus recommendations mandate a strict definition of diagnostic yield, in which only specific malignant diagnoses and specific benign diagnoses sufficient to inform patient care are counted as truly diagnostic. Follow-up data are essential for calculating diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity for malignancy, negative predictive value, and false-negative rates - but should not retroactively reclassify nonspecific or nondiagnostic index results as diagnostic. We propose that the diagnostic process be understood as a chain: tool/access → navigation → position confirmation → sampling → pathology → final clinic-radiologic diagnosis. Failure at any link may create a diagnostic gap and produce a falsely reassuring result. Newer technologies address different links: robotic bronchoscopy primarily narrows the access and stability gap, while CBCT and augmented fluoroscopy primarily narrow the position confirmation gap. Neither technology - alone or combined - closes the sampling, pathology, or clinical concordance gaps. KEY MESSAGES: A benign biopsy result can be trusted only when it is specific, representative, concordant with imaging, and obtained after confirmed lesion access. Nonspecific benign findings, atypia, suspicious results, and nondiagnostic samples should not be considered reassuring when pretest probability remains elevated. Conversely, residual uncertainty should not trigger indefinite escalation. Rational management requires both escalation rules and stopping rules, informed by baseline malignancy risk, biopsy quality, lesion behavior over time, patient fitness, and whether further tissue acquisition is realistically likely to change clinical management.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Automatic event detection (AED) algorithms are proprietary, most available evidence derives from post-market studies, and a comprehensive synthesis of their performance is lacking. METHODS: Pubmed, EMBASE and CENTRAL were searched for studies in OSA adults evaluating: 1) Bland-Altman mean difference between AED-derived (any manufacturer) and manually-scored apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), 2) correlation coefficient between AED-derived and manual AHI, 3) sensitivity/specificity for detecting manually-scored AHI≥5 or ≥10 events/h. Sources of heterogeneity were explored through subgroup analyses and meta-regressions. GRADE was used to rate certainty of evidence (CoE). RESULTS: Automatic and manual scoring of AHI were similar (mean difference [95%CI]; -0.53 [-1.74, 0.57] events/h, P = 0.38, I2 = 98%, N = 23 studies, 1990 participants; CoE: low). Heterogeneity was likely explained by manufacturer, and by a temporal trend towards increasing underestimation (-5.62 [-8.14, -3.10] events/h per decade, P < 0.001). Correlation of AHI between methods was high (0.79 [0.71, 0.84], I2 = 91%, N = 16; CoE: low). Sensitivity was lower than specificity at AHI≥5 (0.82 [0.66, 0.92]; 0.87 [0.82, 0.91]; N = 8) and at AHI≥10 events/h (0.70 [0.56, 0.81]; 0.92 [0.81, 0.97]; N = 9), with low-to-very-low CoE. CONCLUSIONS: AED and manual scoring exhibit comparable metrics, but substantial variability across studies exists. Current devices may underscore AHI and have a non-negligible rate of false negatives.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The real-world effectiveness and safety of consolidation immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) for limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world outcomes of this approach. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients with LS-SCLC who received definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) at two institutions between January 2022 and January 2025. They were grouped by receipt of consolidation immunotherapy (programmed death-ligand 1 [PD-L1] inhibitor) and propensity score matched (1:2). The primary outcome measures were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); the secondary outcome measures were brain metastasis-free survival (BMFS), intrathoracic and extrathoracic PFS, and safety. RESULTS: 211 matched patients were evaluated (non-consolidation immunotherapy, 140; consolidation immunotherapy, 71). The median follow-up was 34.7 months. Consolidation immunotherapy was associated with longer PFS (18.9 vs. 12.1 months; p = 0.026), OS (not reached vs. 31.6 months; p < 0.001), intrathoracic and extrathoracic PFS (p = 0.025 and 0.006) and was an independent prognostic factor for PFS and OS. In exploratory analyses stratified by best response to CRT, consolidation immunotherapy was associated with longer OS in the PR subgroup, but no statistically significant treatment-by-response interaction was observed for either OS or PFS. In the consolidation immunotherapy group, OS was similar across initiation intervals, whereas PFS was most favorable when PD-L1 inhibitors were initiated 4-6 weeks after CRT. Prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) was associated with longer BMFS; safety was comparable between groups. CONCLUSION: Consolidation PD-L1 inhibition after definitive CRT was associated with improved survival and disease control with manageable safety in real-world patients with LS-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The addition of radial endobronchial ultrasound (r-EBUS)-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA) to transbronchial biopsy (TBB) may improve the relationship between the r-EBUS probe and target lesion, helping overcome the limited efficacy of TBB alone. However, the efficacy and safety of this sequential procedure for peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unknown. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance and safety of r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB for PPLs in patients with ILD. METHODS: In a single-center, single-arm, phase Ⅱ trial, patients with PPLs and concomitant ILD were prospectively enrolled to undergo r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB under virtual bronchoscopy navigation and fluoroscopy. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic yield for PPLs. Secondary outcomes included improvement in r-EBUS findings, procedural time, and safety. RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were analyzed, excluding one patient who was found to have an endobronchial lesion during bronchoscopy. The median maximum lesion diameter on computed tomography was 22.3 mm (range: 11.2-70.3 mm). The diagnostic yield for PPLs in patients with ILD was 78.7% (37/47 patients, lower 95% confidence interval: 66.6%, P < 0.001). Improvement in r-EBUS findings during TBNA/TBB procedures was observed in 70.8% (17/24 patients, 95% confidence interval: 48.9-87.4%). The median procedural time was approximately 50 min. Pneumothorax occurred in two patients, one of whom required thoracic drainage. CONCLUSION: This phase II study suggested that sequential r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB might be a useful diagnostic approach for PPLs in patients with ILD, with no serious adverse events observed. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Metastatic dissemination is a major determinant of poor outcome in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, molecular features associated with distinct metastatic states, particularly lymph node and brain metastases, remain incompletely defined. We investigated the relationship between HAX1 and LUAD metastatic progression. METHODS: We reanalyzed publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE131907 to characterize HAX1 expression and associated transcriptional programs across normal lung, primary LUAD, advanced tumors, metastatic lymph nodes (mLN), and brain metastases. Findings were validated using additional public datasets from GEO and TCGA, including the independent single-cell dataset GSE69405. Clinical LUAD specimens were analyzed to assess HAX1 protein expression and its clinicopathological associations. Functional validation was performed in A549 and H1975 cells, and tumor growth was assessed using an A549-derived subcutaneous xenograft model. RESULTS: HAX1 expression and the proportion of HAX1-positive epithelial cells increased across LUAD disease states and were significantly enriched in mLN and brain-metastatic epithelial populations compared with primary tumors. In a 125-patient clinical cohort, high HAX1 expression was associated with lymph node metastasis, advanced stage, and shorter overall survival, and remained independently associated with lymph node metastasis after adjustment for T stage (OR = 2.581, 95% CI 1.161-5.742; P = 0.020). An independent single-cell dataset further confirmed elevated HAX1 expression in brain-metastatic LUAD cells. HAX1-associated transcriptional programs converged on E2F, MYC, MTORC1, DNA replication, and cell-cycle signatures, whereas brain-metastatic epithelial cells additionally exhibited mitochondrial and translational programs. Integrated analyses identified UBE2S, PITX1, GGH, and PDCD2L as HAX1-associated candidates.EPIC and TIMER analyses consistently showed inverse correlations between HAX1 expression and estimated B-cell, CD4+ T-cell, CD8+ T-cell, and macrophage abundance. HAX1 knockdown also reduced cell viability, increased the G0/G1-phase fraction and decreased the S-phase fraction, reduced G1/S-related protein levels and PI3K/AKT signaling, and inhibited subcutaneous xenograft growth. CONCLUSION: HAX1 is closely associated with metastatic progression of LUAD, with strong clinical evidence for lymph node involvement and reproducible enrichment in brain-metastatic epithelial cells. Its associations with cell-cycle programs and immune cell infiltration, together with its functional role in G1/S progression, support further investigation of HAX1 in metastatic adaptation and tumor-immune interactions.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term use of mandibular advancement device (MAD) in a selected phenotype of patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). METHODS: 179 nonobese patients (159 with moderate, 20 with severe OSA) without significant cardiovascular/metabolic comorbidities and/or severe somnolence were prospectively included. Polysomnography was performed at baseline; after 6 months effectiveness of MAD was tested by poly(somno)graphy, Epworth sleepiness score as well as snoring questionnaires. After that, patients were invited annually. RESULTS: Due to loss to follow-up, 31 patients could not be evaluated despite repeated invitations; 2 patients died and 3 patients discontinued because symptoms (including snoring) were no longer bothersome. Within the remaining cohort of 143 patients, 65 (45.5%) discontinued MAD therapy over a 4.5 year observational period. The reasons were an unfavorable balance between perceived benefit and subjective side effects (58.5%) and dental-related problems (41.5%). The only clinically relevant determinant why patients stopped due to an unfavorable benefit-side-effect balance was a higher residual AHI on polysomnography after titration. The proportion of discontinuation attributable to dental issues increased with longer duration of use. Following discontinuation, 73.8% of patients were transitioned to CPAP therapy, with good adherence. CONCLUSIONS: In this predefined OSA phenotype, almost half of the patients stopped MAD after 4.5 years, mainly due to subjective (and objective) inefficacy. However, discontinuation due to tooth movement is also a significant problem; this often goes unnoticed by the patient, and the decision to discontinue treatment is the dentist's responsibility, yet they lack clear guidelines for doing so.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence for home high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) in COPD with chronic respiratory failure remains uncertain. METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, OpenAlex (from 2010) and ClinicalTrials.gov through 1 August 2026, and CENTRAL on 6 November 2026, for randomized trials in adults with COPD and chronic respiratory failure comparing home HFNC (≥4 weeks) with usual care, long-term oxygen therapy or home non-invasive ventilation (NIV). We used Hartung-Knapp random-effects intervals, RoB 2 and GRADE. RESULTS: Six trials (588 participants) differed in hypercapnia selection and clinical stability. All pooled estimates favoured HFNC, but confidence intervals included the null. The moderate-to-severe exacerbation rate ratio was 0.51 (Hartung-Knapp 95% CI 0.01-18.35). Mean differences were -8.83 points (-18.56 to 0.89) on the St George's Respiratory Questionnaire, -2.36 mmHg (-6.71 to 1.99) for daytime PaCO2 and -4.05 mmHg (-14.55 to 6.45) for nocturnal transcutaneous CO2. Evidence for admissions (one trial) and mortality (two trials) was inconclusive. In one six-week crossover trial, CO2 change with HFNC was non-inferior to home NIV within a prespecified 5 mmHg margin. Certainty was low to very low. CONCLUSION: Home HFNC may reduce exacerbations, carbon dioxide and symptom burden in a heterogeneous population with COPD and chronic respiratory failure, but no pooled estimate was statistically robust. Non-inferiority for a physiological surrogate does not establish clinical equivalence with NIV; the review does not establish HFNC as an alternative to NIV and does not support a treatment recommendation. Adequately powered trials in a clearly specified population are needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The 1-year cough duration threshold has been used in clinical trials of refractory chronic cough (RCC), but it has not been validated for a diagnostic or prognostic boundary. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to investigate the association between cough duration and subsequent diagnosis of RCC. METHODS: We analyzed adults with chronic cough enrolled in the prospective, multicenter Korean Chronic Cough Registry. Patients were classified as having recent-onset (8 weeks to ≤ 12 months) or longstanding chronic cough (> 12 months), according to cough duration at enrollment. The primary outcome was a first physician-recorded diagnosis of RCC during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier, restricted cubic spline, and Cox regression analyses were performed. RESULTS: Among 741 patients, 221 had recent-onset chronic cough and 520 had longstanding chronic cough. RCC was diagnosed in 39.6% and 58.1% of these groups, respectively (P < 0.001). 23.1% of patients with recent-onset chronic cough were diagnosed with RCC before their total cough duration exceeded 12 months. Longer cough duration was independently associated with RCC diagnosis (adjusted hazard ratio per doubling, 1.10; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-1.17; P < 0.001), but restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of a discrete threshold at 12 months. Greater baseline cough severity and lower fractional exhaled nitric oxide levels were also associated with RCC diagnosis. CONCLUSION: RCC was diagnosed in a substantial proportion of patients during the first year of chronic cough. These findings suggest that RCC recognition should not be restricted to patients with cough persisting for more than 1 year, while indicating that cough duration carries prognostic information as a continuum.

papers.title_en: Health profiles and asthma-related outcomes among US adults with a history of asthma: A cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Mao S, Wu L
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Paediatrics, Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medici…
papers.results: 2015-2018期：与低共病类比，肥胖代谢类当前哮喘患病率更高（PR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.14）、哮喘发作更高（PR 1.15, 95% CI 1.05-1.26）；肥胖高共病类当前哮喘更高（PR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.18）；吸烟主导类当前哮喘更低（PR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.96）；均q<0.05。2019-2022期：与低共病类比，肥胖主导类当前哮喘更高（PR 1.10, 95% CI 1.05-1.16）、发作更高（PR 1.22, 95% CI 1.09-1.36）；心脏代谢多共病类发作更高（PR 1.40, 95% CI 1.23-1.59）；均q<0.05。两期中女性、COPD、因费用未满足用药需求与三项结局患病率均升高相关（摘要未给数值）；年龄与当前哮喘及发作呈非线性关联（各期非线性P均<0.05）。2015-2018期识别6个潜在类别，2019-2022期4个；bootstrap类别匹配在2019-2022期更一致，部分关联在敏感性分析中存在差异。
papers.authors_conclusion: Obesity-related health profiles were associated current asthma and attack, while cost-related unmet medication need was associated with all three asthma-related outcomes. These findings highlight the relevance of considering coexisting health conditions and medication affordability when assessing the needs of adults with a history of a history of asthma.
papers.ai_note: 横断面设计仅得患病率关联，不能推断因果或时序，潜在类别与哮喘谁先谁后无法确定。两期类别数不同（6 vs 4），跨期类别不可直接比较，而结论将两期结果合并表述。吸烟主导类当前哮喘患病率反而更低（PR 0.89）与常识相悖，可能为诊断偏倚/吸烟者就医与哮喘诊断不足所致，摘要未讨论。摘要明确提示部分关联在敏感性分析中不一致，但结论未体现该不稳定性。费用相关未满足用药需求与三项结局的关联为作者结论重点之一，但摘要未给出该因素的任何PR/CI数值，信息不足。研究非胸肿瘤领域，与胸部肿瘤临床业务关联有限。

pico.ic: 暴露为潜在健康谱类别（肥胖代谢类、肥胖高共病类、吸烟主导类、肥胖主导类、心脏代谢多共病类等），对照为低共病类；结局为当前哮喘、过去一年哮喘发作、哮喘相关急诊或紧急就诊；未设干预

papers.reason: 为哮喘合并症管理与用药可及性问题提供人群层面的横断面证据基线，并展示LCA+FDR控制在多组比较中的应用范式，可作为呼吸慢病队列设计的方法学参考，但不改变肿瘤方向的临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: BackgroundAssociation between health profiles with asthma-related outcomes among adults with a history of asthma remain incompletely understood.ObjectivesTo identify latent health profiles and examine their associations with asthma-related outcomes among US adults with a history of asthma.DesignPopulation-based cross-sectional study using National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) data from 2015-2018 and 2019-2022 were analysed separately.MethodsWe analysed 14,386 participants from 2015-2018 and 13,924 from 2019-2022. Latent class analysis (LCA) included obesity, current smoking, and seven chronic conditions. Survey-weighted modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) for current asthma, past-year asthma attack, and asthma-related emergency room (ER) or urgent-care visit. The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure controlled the false discovery rate (FDR) across 24 primary class comparisons. Exploratory individual-factor analyses and restricted cubic splines (RCS) examined the associations with individual characteristics and age. Sensitivity analyses included alternative age and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) adjustments, logistic standardization, fixed-measurement two-step estimation and 100 primary sampling unit bootstrap replicates per period.ResultsLCA identified six profiles in 2015-2018 and four in 2019-2022. In 2015-2018, compared with the low-multimorbidity class, the obesity-metabolic class had higher prevalences of current asthma (PR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.14) and attack (PR 1.15, 95% CI 1.05-1.26), while the obesity-high-multimorbidity class had higher current asthma prevalence (PR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.18). The smoking-predominant class had lower current asthma prevalence (PR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.96; all q<0.05). In 2019-2022, compared with the low-multimorbidity class, the obesity-predominant class had higher prevalences of current asthma (PR 1.10, 95% CI 1.05-1.16) and attack (PR 1.22, 95% CI 1.09-1.36), while the cardiometabolic multimorbidity class had higher attack prevalence (PR 1.40, 95% CI 1.23-1.59; all q< 0.05). Female sex, COPD, and unmet medication need due to cost were associated with higher prevalences of all three asthma-related outcomes in both periods. Age showed nonlinear associations with current asthma and attack in both periods (all P for nonlinearity <0.05). Bootstrap class matching was more consistent in 2019-2022, although some associations varied across sensitivity analyses.ConclusionsObesity-related health profiles were associated current asthma and attack, while cost-related unmet medication need was associated with all three asthma-related outcomes. These findings highlight the relevance of considering coexisting health conditions and medication affordability when assessing the needs of adults with a history of asthma.

papers.abstract_en: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) serve as a critical first line of defence against respiratory pathogens and ensure lung function during both infection and steady-state conditions. They express several surface markers, including epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM, also known as CD326), whose role remains unclear. Here we show that EpCAM is a distinct surface marker of fetal-derived AMs, distinguishing them from other tissue-resident macrophages. Although it is dispensable for their homeostatic function, it contributes to efficient uptake and timely clearance of respiratory bacterial pathogens including Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila. During influenza infection, EpCAM is rapidly downregulated in AMs via TNF-mediated NF-κB signalling, and the Epcam locus undergoes sustained chromatin repression and epigenetic remodelling. Its downregulation persists after viral clearance, and AMs from virus-infected mice show significantly reduced bacterial uptake. This suggests that viral infection reprogrammes AMs, contributing to increased susceptibility to secondary bacterial infection. These findings uncover a previously unknown role for EpCAM and highlight its potential impact on AM phenotypic plasticity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nocturnal intermittent hypoxia (IH) is a hallmark feature of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and contributes to oxidative stress and inflammation, which in turn may accelerate biological aging. Epigenetic clocks can estimate biological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is greater severity of IH associated with increased biological aging? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We studied adults referred for suspected OSA in a multisite sleep and circadian research network, a cross-sectional observational cohort (2016-2021). IH severity was assessed using the 4% oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from home sleep apnea testing or in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG). DNAm from peripheral blood leukocytes was assayed using Illumina EPIC arrays. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and pace of aging were calculated using multiple DNAm clocks. Linear regression models were adjusted for leukocyte composition, age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, smoking, site, alcohol, diabetes, and hypertension. A false discovery rate of 0.05 was used. RESULTS: A total of 1364 participants were included (median age, 56 yrs; median ODI, 16/h; median BMI, 32 kg/m2; 57% male). Higher ODI was associated with EAA for PhenoAge (β = 0.028, adjusted P = .0048) and with pace of aging (DunedinPACE, β = 0.0005, adjusted P =.0012). No significant associations were observed for first-generation clocks. INTERPRETATION: Greater IH severity, as assessed by ODI, was independently associated with increased biological aging as measured by PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks. These findings support a link between OSA and biological aging, raising the possibility of using epigenetic age measures as biomarkers of OSA-related morbidity.

papers.authors: Wang J, Zheng H, Li H, Sun L, Yiminniyaze R, Wang S, Li X, Zheng S et al.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a rare large-vessel vasculitis, and pulmonary artery involvement (PAI) can cause severe stenosis and pulmonary hypertension (PH), markedly impairing exercise capacity and quality of life. Although balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) has emerged as a promising interventional option, its preliminary efficacy and safety in TA-PAI-particularly in patients without PH-remain insufficiently defined. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the preliminary safety and differential clinical outcomes of BPA in patients with TA-PAI, stratified by the presence or absence of baseline PH. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed TA-PAI patients undergoing BPA. Hemodynamics, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), exercise capacity, and Quality of Life (QoL) were assessed pre- and post-BPA. Lesion anatomy and procedural complications were recorded. Statistical analyses compared PH and without PH subgroups. RESULTS: Among 33 TA-PAI patients, including 22 with PH and 11 without PH, BPA significantly reduced mPAP (25.41 ± 8.86 to 22.82 ± 7.94 mmHg, P = 0.005) and Pulmonary Vascular Resistance (PVR) from ( 3.06 [1.37,6.04] to 2.17 [1.35, 4.28] WU, P=0.039) in the overall population. In the PH subgroup, significant hemodynamic and functional improvements were observed, including reduced NT-proBNP (P=0.024), increased 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) (P=0.012), and enhanced QoL (all P <0.001). Conversely, the without PH group showed no significant hemodynamic changes (P > 0.05) but demonstrated modest 6MWD increases and significant QoL improvements. Left pulmonary artery lesions were more prevalent in the PH group (42.0% vs. 5.7%, P < 0.001). The procedure was generally safe, with infrequent complications, including vascular dissection (1.6%) and haemoptysis (0.8%), occurring only in a small number of patients. CONCLUSIONS: BPA demonstrated acceptable safety and preliminary efficacy for symptomatic TA-PAI. Findings suggest preliminary functional and hemodynamic benefits in patients with baseline PH, whereas benefits in patients without PH were primarily limited to quality of life rather than hemodynamics. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.authors: Lee GI, Na MS, Oh H, Seo JM, Shin S, Kim WI, Jeong HY, Park DS et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: The Korean Institute of Tuberculosis, Korea National Tuberculosis Association, 168-5, Osongsaengmyeong4-ro, Osong-eup, C…
papers.results: 共检出31例菌学确诊结核，筛查检出率119.8例/10万人，NNS 835（95% CI 588-1,229）；男性检出率高于女性（229.2 vs 72.1/10万，p<0.001），75-79岁组最高；确诊病例中51.6%归为非活动性结核，16.1%胸片正常；19.4%存在耐药，全部为异烟肼耐药；多因素分析：男性（AOR 2.395；95% CI 1.113-5.154）、结核相关影像学表现（AOR 26.686；95% CI 8.311-85.687）、胸片提示其他疾病（AOR 7.117；95% CI 2.067-24.503）、咳嗽（AOR 5.285；95% CI 1.995-14.001）、咳痰（AOR 3.157；95% CI 1.312-7.598）与结核检出独立相关

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) in Korea is increasingly concentrated among older adults. We evaluated a senior community center-based TB screening program in Jeollanam-do Province, southwestern Korea. METHODS: Between January 2023 and December 2024, community-based TB screening was conducted at senior community centers, primarily targeting adults aged ≥65 years. Screening included chest radiography, a structured questionnaire, and sputum examination when indicated. TB was confirmed by smear microscopy, culture, and molecular tests. Detection yield, number needed to screen (NNS), and associated factors were analyzed and compared with previous elderly TB screening programs in Korea using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 25,885 participants (mean age, 76.6±7.7 years; 69.7% female), 31 bacteriologically confirmed TB cases were identified, yielding 119.8 cases per 100,000 screened and an NNS of 835 (95% CI, 588-1,229). Detection rates were higher in males than females (229.2 vs. 72.1 per 100,000; p<0.001) and highest among those aged 75-79 years. Among confirmed cases, 51.6% were classified as Inactive TB and 16.1% had Normal chest radiographs. Drug resistance was identified in 19.4% of cases, all involving isoniazid resistance. Male sex (AOR, 2.395; 95% CI, 1.113-5.154), TB-related radiographic findings (AOR, 26.686; 95% CI, 8.311-85.687), other diseases suspected on chest radiography (AOR, 7.117; 95% CI, 2.067-24.503), cough (AOR, 5.285; 95% CI, 1.995-14.001), and sputum production (AOR, 3.157; 95% CI, 1.312-7.598) were independently associated with TB detection. CONCLUSION: Senior community center-based screening achieved a high detection yield and low NNS. Detection of bacteriologically confirmed TB across diverse radiographic categories supports an integrated screening strategy combining chest radiography, symptom assessment, and microbiological evaluation in older adults.

papers.title_en: Collagen remodeling is elevated in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis and may distinguish it from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.authors: Christoforidou G, Simões FB, Dræby SD, Kronborg-White S, Hoyer N, Karsdal MA, Leeming DJ, Bendstrup E et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Biomedical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark.
papers.results: PFBIO-non-fHP较健康对照血清C3M升高（95%CI: 0.34-0.56, p<0.0001）、C6M升高（0.46-0.81, p=0.001）；PFBIO-fHP较健康对照C3M升高（0.31-0.51, p<0.0001）、C6M升高（0.47-0.82, p=0.001）；fHP与non-fHP之间标志物水平无差异。PFBIO队列IPF较fHP的PRO-C3升高（0.68-0.99, p=0.038）、PRO-C6升高（0.56-0.83, p=0.0002）、C6M升高（0.47-0.76, p<0.0001）；验证队列AUH中仅PRO-C3在IPF较fHP显著升高（1.004-1.353, p=0.044）。
papers.authors_conclusion: HP血清III型和VI型胶原重塑标志物显著高于健康人，且与是否存在纤维化无关，提示疾病中ECM重塑增加；这些标志物在一个队列中IPF较fHP升高。研究结果提示III型和VI型胶原重塑标志物反映HP中活跃的ECM转换，并可能与现有标准联合用于临床区分fHP与IPF。
papers.ai_note: 验证队列仅PRO-C3复现，PRO-C6与C6M均未复现，但结论笼统称'这些标志物在IPF中较fHP升高'，属对未复现结果的选择性概括；标题与结论使用'distinguish/may be used to differentiate'，但摘要未报告任何诊断准确性指标（AUC、敏感度、特异度、阈值），区分能力信息不足；各标志物效应量CI为比值型数值但摘要未标明量纲与分析方法（是否校正年龄、吸烟、肾功能等）；样本量小（每组21-46例）且为横断面设计，无法评估纵向预后价值；另C6M在HP中高于健康人却仅在一个队列中IPF>fHP，生物学解释信息不足。

papers.reason: 影响间质性肺疾病中fHP与IPF的鉴别诊断路径——若成立可为无法明确抗原暴露的纤维化HP患者避免误诊为IPF而延误抗纤维化或免疫抑制决策，但因缺乏诊断准确性指标且验证不完全，目前仅可作为研究设计参考与假设生成。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (fHP) are two common causes of pulmonary fibrosis. Unlike IPF, fHP is caused by a persistent immune response to an antigen. Misclassification of fHP and IPF can lead to significant delays in antifibrotic treatment, particularly in cases where the eliciting antigen cannot be identified and removed. Extracellular matrix (ECM) and, particularly, collagen remodeling is a key feature of fibrosis. We characterized ECM remodeling in HP phenotypes by quantifying serological biomarkers of type III and VI collagen turnover in comparison to healthy controls. We then evaluated the potential of these biomarkers as tools to differentiate fHP from IPF in two separate independent cohorts. METHODS: Biomarkers of type III and VI collagen formation (nordicPRO-C3™ and nordicPRO-C6™) and degradation (nordicC3M™ and nordicC6M™) were quantified cross-sectionally in serum from PFBIO-HP (NCT05549635, PFBIO-non-fHP; n = 25, PFBIO-fHP; n = 24) and healthy controls (n = 20). Biomarkers were then compared between the HP phenotypes and IPF patients from PFBIO (NCT02755441, n = 46). Findings were validated in an independent cohort, (AUH-ILD, NCT05311345, AUH-IPF; n = 43, AUH-fHP; n = 21). RESULTS: Serum C3M and C6M were elevated compared to healthy in PFBIO-non-fHP (C3M 95% CI: 0.34-0.56, p < 0.0001 and C6M: 0.46-0.81, p = 0.001) and PFBIO-fHP (C3M: 0.31-0.51, p < 0.0001, C6M: 0.47-0.82, p = 0.001). Biomarker levels did not differ between fHP and non-fHP. Serum PRO-C3, PRO-C6 and C6M were elevated in PFBIO-IPF compared to PFBIO-fHP (PRO-C3: 0.68-0.99, p = 0.038, PRO-C6: 0.56-0.83, p = 0.0002, C6M: 0.47-0.76, p < 0.0001), whereas only PRO-C3 was significantly elevated in AUH-IPF compared to AUH-fHP (1.004-1.353, p = 0.044). CONCLUSIONS: Serological biomarkers of type III and VI collagen remodeling were significantly elevated in HP compared to healthy, regardless of fibrosis status, suggestive of an increased ECM remodeling in the disease. Furthermore, these biomarkers were elevated in IPF compared to fHP in a cohort of both diagnoses. Our findings suggest that type III and VI collagen remodeling biomarkers are reflective of active ECM turnover in HP and may also be used alongside existing criteria to differentiate between fHP and IPF in the clinic.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet early diagnosis remains challenging due to limited access to spirometry in many clinical settings. The Lead I electrocardiographic sign, which is defined by an isoelectric P wave, reduced QRS amplitude, and diminished T-wave amplitude in lead I, has been reported in association with COPD. This study evaluated the association between the Lead I sign and COPD in adults aged 30-70 years. METHODS: A retrospective case-control study was conducted at a Midwestern community hospital between 2014 and 2024. Patients were classified by Lead I sign status (positive vs. negative) and COPD status (present vs. absent). COPD-positive patients were identified by post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC < 0.70 on spirometry, or CT findings suggestive of COPD. Multivariable logistic regression was performed adjusting for age, sex, BMI, smoking history, pack-years greater than 20, hypertension, coronary artery disease, heart failure, and hypothyroidism. RESULTS: Among 201 patients, COPD was present in 83.3% of Lead I positive patients compared with 11.4% of Lead I negative patients (p < 0.001). The Lead I sign demonstrated sensitivity 87.0% (95% CI 78.6-92.4%), specificity 85.3% (95% CI 77.5-90.8%), PPV 83.3% (95% CI 74.6-89.5%), and NPV 88.6% (95% CI 81.1-93.3%). On multivariable logistic regression, COPD was the sole independent predictor of Lead I sign positivity (adjusted OR 40.6, 95% CI 17.6-104, p < 0.001). No cardiovascular or metabolic covariate reached significance after adjustment. CONCLUSION: The Lead I sign demonstrates a strong and independent association with COPD after comprehensive confounder adjustment. It is suggestive of but not diagnostic of COPD and is not intended to replace spirometry. Its presence on a routinely obtained ECG may serve as a diagnostic clue to prompt further pulmonary evaluation, particularly where spirometry access is limited.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sarcoidosis is a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown origin, primarily affecting the lungs and lymphatic system. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, histological confirmation of non-necrotizing granulomas, and exclusion of other conditions. However, current diagnostic methods are invasive and costly, making them unsuitable for disease monitoring. Existing biomarkers lack accuracy and clinical utility. The objective was to evaluate exhaled breath analysis as a noninvasive, real-time diagnostic and monitoring tool for pulmonary sarcoidosis, by identifying disease-specific metabolic signatures. METHODS: Exhaled breath samples were collected from patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis, matched controls without lung disease, and patients with pulmonary fibrosis. Patients with sarcoidosis were further stratified into active and inactive disease states. Molecular breath profiles were compared using t test and prediction models were developed based on ReliefF feature selection and Naïve Bayes algorithms. RESULTS: Thirty-nine patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis, 39 matched controls, and 25 patients with pulmonary fibrosis were included. Sarcoidosis could be discriminated from matched controls with a repeated cross-validated receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.76, with the main metabolic changes in fatty acid and cysteine metabolism. Active sarcoidosis was discriminated from inactive disease with a repeated cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.77, with linoleate metabolism playing a central role. CONCLUSION: Exhaled breath analysis shows potential to distinguish patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis from matched controls and patients with pulmonary fibrosis, and to differentiate between active and inactive sarcoidosis. Metabolic signatures, particularly involving fatty acid and linoleate metabolism, support its potential as a noninvasive, real-time tool for diagnosis and monitoring of pulmonary sarcoidosis, pending validation in larger cohorts. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05458934) at 14/07/2022.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the discrimination value of inflammatory biomarkers for frailty in hospitalised elderly adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and explore the relationship between inflammatory markers and frailty in elderly adults. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among elderly inpatients with COPD admitted to a tertiary hospital between March 2024 and June 2025. Frailty was evaluated using the Fried phenotype. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify independent risk associated with frailty. Spearman correlation analyses and sensitivity analyses were performed to explore the relationship between inflammatory makers and frailty and assess the diagnostic value of inflammatory makers. RESULTS: Among 553 hospitalised elderly patients with COPD, 35.98% (n = 199) were frail. Activities of Daily Living (ADL), GOLD rank and C-reactive protein (CRP), absolute neutrophil count (ANC) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) were identified as independent risk factors of frailty. Correlation analyses showed that CRP, ANC, procalcitonin (PCT), white blood cell (WBC) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) were significantly associated with frailty. Sensitivity analyses revealed that adding WBC, PCT and ESR modestly improved basic model's performance, confirming the diagnostic value of these markers. CONCLUSION: Frailty in elderly COPD patients is strongly correlated with inflammation indicators. Integrating inflammatory biomarkers and disease-specific clinical characteristics can enhance frailty risk discrimination accuracy in this study. Even non-independent inflammatory risk factors retain notable clinical associations with frailty, and an expanded panel of such markers may provide a more objective basis for early identification and targeted management of high-risk elderly COPD patients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management is increasingly supported by application-based mobile health (mHealth) interventions. However, their effects on acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD)-related hospitalization and other health outcomes remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of application-based mHealth interventions in people with COPD. METHODS: This review followed the Cochrane Handbook and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL Ultimate, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from inception to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials involving adults with COPD were included if the intervention was delivered through a mobile-device application and compared with usual care without application-based mHealth support. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias 2 tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. RESULTS: Eighteen studies reported in 19 publications were included. Application-based mHealth interventions did not significantly reduce the number of participants with AECOPD-related hospitalization (RR = 0.97; 95% CI = 0.78 to 1.20) or improve quality of life measured by the Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire (MD = - 0.08; 95% CI = - 0.51 to 0.35) or St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (MD = - 2.90; 95% CI = - 7.24 to 1.43). In contrast, these interventions improved functional exercise capacity, as reflected by increased 6-minute walk distance (MD = 32.20 m; 95% CI = 13.44 to 50.96). Studies assessing psychological status using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale reported no significant between-group differences. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not clearly support application-based mHealth as an effective strategy for reducing AECOPD-related hospitalization or improving quality of life in people with COPD. However, it may have potential for improving functional exercise capacity. Future trials should more clearly define application functions, intervention frameworks, and target populations to determine when, for whom, and through which mechanisms application-based mHealth can improve clinically meaningful outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) cause avoidable mortality, yet the basic health-system capacity needed for diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment is unevenly distributed. We assessed global variation in technical respiratory care readiness and its relationship with asthma and COPD mortality. METHODS: We conducted an ecological, cross-sectional analysis of 200 countries using WHO-linked public datasets and World Bank income classifications. Technical respiratory care readiness was defined using five country-level indicators: bronchodilator inhalers, steroid inhalers, budesonide-formoterol inhalers, peak-flow measurement, and spirometry. Primary outcomes were 2021 age-standardised asthma and COPD mortality rates. Log-linear models estimated associations between readiness and mortality, adjusted for tobacco use, clean-fuel access, and World Bank income group. A burden-readiness typology identified countries with high combined asthma/COPD mortality and low readiness. RESULTS: Technical readiness data were available for 192 countries; 155 countries had complete data for adjusted models. Median technical readiness was 4.0 of 5 components (IQR 2.0-5.0), equivalent to 80.0% readiness (IQR 40.0-100.0). Readiness was lowest in low-income countries and highest in high-income countries. Low-income countries had limited availability of budesonide-formoterol inhalers (5%), spirometry (7%), peak-flow measurement (21%), steroid inhalers (35%), and bronchodilator inhalers (46%). The estimated percentage changes in mortality per 10%-point increase in technical readiness were -2.1% for asthma mortality (95% CI -7.6 to 3.8), -0.7% for COPD mortality (-4.4 to 3.1), and -0.6% for combined mortality (-4.2 to 3.0); all confidence intervals included the null. The typology identified 21 high-burden/low-readiness countries. CONCLUSION: The adjusted analyses did not show statistically significant independent associations between technical readiness and mortality. Descriptive burden-readiness mapping identified countries where high asthma/COPD mortality coincided with weak reported availability of essential inhaled medicines and basic diagnostic tools. These observations support readiness-burden mapping as a prioritisation approach for more detailed assessment of chronic respiratory care capacity.

papers.authors: Mandin V, Hassoun D, Habeau R, Moui A, Menigoz C, Sagan C, Liberge R, Blanc FX et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Nantes Université, CHU Nantes, Service de Pneumologie, L'institut Du thorax, Nantes, France.
papers.results: PPF表型者基线BE水平显著更高：中位0.28 G/L（p = 0.0087）。以0.3 G/L为界，BE > 0.3 G/L者PFS更短：417天 vs BE ≤ 0.3 G/L者763天（p = 0.0068）。校正年龄、性别及基线FVC后该关联仍显著（HR 2.85；95% CI, 1.53-5.28；p < 0.001）。

papers.abstract_en: ObjectivesPreclinical studies support the involvement of type 2-driven inflammation, with eosinophils as key cellular players, in the pathophysiology of fibrogenesis. However, data on blood eosinophils (BE) distribution at baseline and their prognostic impact in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (fHP) are lacking.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study including adult patients with a multidisciplinary-confirmed diagnosis of fHP between 2016 and 2022. BE levels at baseline were assessed, along with their association with the following outcomes: disease progression, death, or acute exacerbation. Clinical, biological, functional, and imaging data were collected over two years after baseline assessment. Progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) was defined according to criteria used in the INBUILD trial. Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model based on a composite endpoint (progression or death).Results70 patients were included. Those with a PPF phenotype had significantly higher BE levels at baseline: median 0.28 G/L (p = 0.0087). Using a 0.3 G/L cutoff, PFS was shorter in patients with BE > 0.3 G/L: 417 days versus 763 days for those with BE ≤ 0.3 G/L (p = 0.0068). This association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex and baseline FVC (HR 2.85; 95% CI, 1.53-5.28; p < 0.001).ConclusionIn this single-center cohort, BE counts at baseline differed according to PPF phenotype identified during follow-up. Reduced PFS was observed when BE counts exceeded 0.3 G/L, indicating a higher risk of progression or death. These findings require further prospective confirmation with longitudinal BE assessment.

papers.authors: Wang J, Li J, Peng J, Zhang M, Wang X, Akinyemi AO, Alam MR, Howlader M et al.

papers.abstract_en: Cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), a serine/threonine kinase essential for cell cycle progression, also plays critical roles in DNA damage response, gene expression regulation, and therapeutic resistance. In this study, we identify a previously unrecognized regulatory link between CDK1 and apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Both CDK1 and APE1 are highly expressed in lung tumors and exhibit an inverse correlation in protein expression levels across multiple lung cancer cell lines. Mechanistically, CDK1 phosphorylates APE1 at Ser54 to promote its degradation, whereas inhibition of CDK1 stabilizes APE1 protein levels and reduces the efficacy of APE1-targeted therapy. Importantly, activation of CDK1 through WEE1 inhibition using MK1775 enhances APE1 degradation and markedly sensitizes NSCLC cells to APE1 inhibition, inducing synthetic lethality. CDK1-mediated APE1 degradation mimics APE1 loss, leading to genome instability, cell-cycle dysregulation, and altered metastatic behavior. Notably, the effect of CDK1-mediated APE1 phosphorylation on cell motility is p53-dependent: in p53-proficient cells, phosphorylated APE1 activates p53-dependent programs that suppress migration and invasion, whereas in p53-deficient cells the same modification enhances metastatic potential. Furthermore, further investigation revealed that APE1 deficiency activates the cGAS-STING pathway and induces PD-L1 expression through the MAPK-ERK axis, thereby reshaping the tumor immune microenvironment and enhancing sensitivity to immune checkpoint blockade. Given the dual roles of CDK1 in APE1 regulation and immune modulation, we propose that a sequential or combinatorial strategy in which WEE1 inhibition activates CDK1 to promote APE1 degradation, priming cancer cells for APE1 inhibition and inducing synthetic lethality, while minimizing toxicity to normal cells. This approach simultaneously disrupts APE1's endonuclease and homologous recombination repair functions and exploits CDK1-driven immune reprogramming to potentiate anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy. Collectively, our findings establish CDK1-mediated APE1 phosphorylation as a key node linking DNA repair, immune evasion, and therapeutic response, and providing a mechanistic rationale for combined CDK1-APE1-PD-L1-targeted therapy in NSCLC.

papers.authors: Fernandes M, Testone G, Bergamo G, Avvento F, Albanesi G, Centonze D, Liguori C

papers.abstract_en: Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA, REM-OSA) is a phenotype in which obstructive respiratory events occur mainly during REM sleep, and may be associated with distinct daytime consequences. This study investigated the neurocognitive, behavioural, subjective sleep and polysomnographic profile of REM-OSA. Patients were classified as having REM-OSA when the REM Apnoea-Hypopnea Index (AHI)/Non-REM (NREM) AHI ratio was ≥ 2 and were compared with patients whose respiratory events predominantly occurred during NREM sleep (NREM-OSA). Patients evaluated for suspected OSA underwent a neuropsychological battery, including the Mini-Mental State Examination, Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test, Digit Span Forward/Backward, Trail Making Test (TMT), Frontal Assessment Battery and Raven's Coloured Progressive Matrices, together with questionnaires evaluating sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), impulsivity (Barratt Impulsiveness Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Of the 91 eligible patients, 17 had mild OSA and were included in sensitivity analyses, while the primary analysis included 74 patients with moderate-to-severe OSA. Thirteen (17.6%) met REM-OSA criteria, and 61 were classified as NREM-OSA. REM-OSA patients had lower overall AHI and oxygen desaturation index and, after False Discovery Rate correction, longer TMT-A, TMT-B and TMT B-A (all q = 0.003). After adjustment for depressive symptoms, REM-OSA independently predicted longer TMT-A (β = 0.298, p = 0.002), TMT-B (β = 0.235, p = 0.016), TMT B-A (β = 0.258, p = 0.018) and higher impulsivity (β = 0.237, p = 0.043), but not global PSQI scores (β = 0.210, p = 0.086). Sensitivity analyses confirmed poorer TMT-A performance in REM-OSA. These results highlight the neurocognitive relevance of REM phenotype despite lower overall respiratory severity.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic respiratory diseases (CRDs) substantially contribute to India's non-communicable disease burden, especially in rural populations. Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) is useful for community-based respiratory screening in resource-limited settings. This community-based cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of impaired expiratory airflow among rural adults aged ≥30 years in Western India. Data were collected through house-to-house visits using a structured questionnaire administered by trained ASHA workers. Information regarding sociodemographic, environmental risk factors and comorbidities was obtained. PEFR was measured using peak flow meters following standard guidelines. A total of 11,359 rural adults participated in the study. Overall, 9.17% of participants had suspected PEFR impairment. The prevalence of PEFR impairment was significantly higher among older adults, males, smokers, underweight individuals, participants using unclean cooking fuel, and those with CRDs, hypertension, or diabetes mellitus. Community-based PEFR screening conducted by ASHA workers may represent a cost-effective strategy for early identification of airflow limitation in rural primary-care settings.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiovascular disease is major determinant of morbidity and mortality in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), yet cardiopulmonary risk remains underrecognized and insufficiently addressed, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). We developed a multidisciplinary consensus to provide practical recommendations for the identification, assessment, and management of cardiopulmonary risk in COPD, adapted to healthcare systems in emerging countries. A modified Delphi process was conducted by a six-member steering committee and a multidisciplinary panel of 21 experts in pulmonology, cardiology and internal medicine. Clinical questions were developed from unmet needs in COPD care and informed by a systematic literature review of studies published between January 2020 and September 2025. Recommendations were graded according to the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) methodology and refined through two Delphi rounds with consensus defined as ≥80% agreement. Thirteen recommendations achieved consensus, including 12 (92.3%) with very strong consensus (≥90% agreement) and one (7.7%) with strong consensus (80-90% agreement). The recommendations address three clinical domains: identification and assessment of respiratory and cardiovascular comorbidities, targeted diagnostic testing, and implementation of evidence-based pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. This modified Delphi consensus provides a practical framework to support systematic cardiopulmonary risk assessment and individualized management of COPD. Although developed for Mexico, its resource-sensitive approach may facilitate implementation across Latin America and other low- and middle-income countries facing similar healthcare challenges.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a life-threatening condition often diagnosed late due to non-specific symptoms and overlapping comorbidities with other cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. Although there have been advances in treatment, diagnostic delays are common, and patients are treated late in their disease course. Investigating the temporal ordering of recorded comorbidities may provide insight into diagnostic patterns associated with delayed PH recognition and adverse outcomes. METHODS: We identified 2,727 PH patients from the UK Biobank cohort of 440,014 participants with diseases diagnoses, and sampled two demographics-matched cohorts of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and heart failure (HF) with the same number of patients as the PH cohort but were not diagnosed with PH. Employing process mining, a methodology originating from business process analysis to extract temporal patterns from event logs, the temporal diagnostic sequences of comorbidity combinations preceding PH diagnosis were compared to those sequences in patients who received a final diagnosis COPD or HF. We also assessed the relative risk of mortality given different combinations of comorbidities and the genetic correlation between comorbidities. RESULTS: Patients diagnosed with PH had prior diagnoses of hypertension (58.1%), atrial fibrillation (31.2%), and heart failure (43.2%). Process mining revealed that the temporal order of cardiometabolic comorbidities influences the timing to diagnosis of PH, COPD and HF. Patients in which type 2 diabetes was diagnosed before systemic hypertension had received PH diagnosis 2 years and 9 months faster than the reverse sequence, where hypertension preceded diabetes. For patients with a final diagnosis of PH, HF and COPD, diagnostic sequences in which hypercholesterolemia was recorded before systemic hypertension and type 2 diabetes were associated with shorter median intervals to PH diagnosis. A sequence involving diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was associated with a significantly higher mortality risk (HR = 1.97; P = 0.001). Additional mortality risk factors included specific orderings of metabolic conditions and comorbidity clusters. CONCLUSION: Temporal diagnostic sequences of comorbidities were associated with the timing of PH diagnosis. Our findings suggest that the presentation and ordering of metabolic diseases may serve as hypothesis-generating epidemiological indicators of PH risk. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) are common among middle-aged and older men and can coexist clinically. However, the direction of causality and the underlying biological links between them remain unclear. METHODS: The population-level association between COPD and BPH was evaluated using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), and Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal directions and immune-related genetic features. We integrated transcriptomic analyses of both diseases and used differential expression, functional enrichment, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning to characterize disease-associated transcriptional profiles and identify shared candidate genes. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses were further used to determine the cellular localization of the key candidate, characterize associated functional states, and assess potential cell-cell interactions. Finally, core mechanisms were validated through co-culture, immunofluorescence, and other experiments. RESULTS: NHANES analysis showed that COPD was significantly associated with prevalent BPH. MR supported a causal effect of COPD on BPH risk; this finding remained stable in multivariable analyses, whereas reverse MR showed no clear effect. Immunogenetic analyses suggested partially overlapping immune features in the two diseases, and transcriptomic findings further converged on immune-inflammatory and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling-related changes. VCAN was identified as a shared key candidate gene that was consistently upregulated in both diseases and validated in external cohorts. Single-cell analysis showed that VCAN was expressed predominantly in prostatic fibroblasts; high VCAN expression was associated with higher inflammatory response and ECM remodeling scores and with predicted communication and spatial associations with macrophages. In vitro, co-culture with M1-like macrophages enhanced VCAN expression, proliferation, and ECM remodeling-related phenotypes in WPMY-1 cells, whereas VCAN silencing attenuated these changes. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence that COPD increases BPH risk and suggests that the two diseases have partially shared immune-inflammatory and ECM remodeling features. VCAN may contribute to prostatic stromal cell proliferation and ECM remodeling induced by macrophage-associated inflammation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUNDS: The application of cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) for assessing heart rate recovery at 1 min (HRR1) is of significant clinical value in evaluating disease severity, cardiovascular risk, and prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases. However, its utility in patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is still understudied. OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations of abnormal HRR1 with Pulmonary Function Test (PFT), modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score, systemic inflammatory markers, as well as acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) during a 1-year follow-up in patients with stable COPD. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed clinical data from 90 patients with stable COPD attending the outpatient clinic of the Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine at China-Japan Friendship Hospital from January 2021 to October 2025. Abnormal HRR1 post-CPET was defined as ≤ 12 beats/min. Patients were then categorized into normal (HRR1 > 12 beats/min) and abnormal (HRR1 ≤ 12 beats/min) groups accordingly. We compared clinical parameters between the two groups and performed multivariable regression analysis to identify independent indicators of adverse outcomes. RESULTS: During the one-year follow-up, patients with abnormal HRR1 exhibited a clinically significant deterioration, including a median increase of 2 points in CAT score, a decline in FEV1 by 110 ml, and a reduction in FEV1pred by 3.656%. Additionally, 68.9% of patients experienced at least one AECOPD. Multivariable regression analysis revealed that HRR1 was an independent indicator of AECOPD and CAT score elevation. Specifically, compared with patients with normal HRR1, those with baseline HRR1 ≤ 12 beats/min exhibited 3.224-fold higher odds of subsequent AECOPD and 1.020-fold higher odds of CAT score worsening. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that HRR1 is associated with airflow limitation, exercise capacity, and systemic inflammation in patients with stable COPD. Furthermore, HRR1 served as an independent indicator of AECOPD and CAT score elevation. A baseline HRR1 cutoff of ≤ 12 beats/min was associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes and greater symptom burden, supporting its potential utility in identifying patients who may benefit from close clinical monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Impaired alveolar fluid clearance (AFC) is a major pathological feature of acute lung injury (ALI). The epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) and Na+/K+-ATPase are the principal ion transport proteins that mediate AFC. Isthmin-1 (ISM1), a secreted protein with diverse biological functions, has been reported to protect against ALI; however, whether this protective effect is mediated through modulation of AFC remains unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the role and mechanism of ISM1 in regulating AFC in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI. METHODS: In vivo, ISM1 was overexpressed in mice using an adeno-associated virus serotype 5 (AAV5) vector, and an anti-GRP78 blocking antibody was administered to neutralize cell-surface GRP78 function. In vitro, LPS-stimulated A549 cells were treated with recombinant ISM1 protein, anti-GRP78 antibody, or the PI3K activator 740Y-P. The severity of ALI was assessed by hematoxylin-eosin staining, lung wet/dry weight ratio, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid total protein concentration, and inflammatory cytokine levels. α-ENaC and Na+/K+-ATPase α1 expression were evaluated by Western blot, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence, and PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway activity was analyzed in both models. RESULTS: ISM1 overexpression attenuated LPS-induced ALI, as shown by reduced lung injury scores, lung wet/dry weight ratios, BALF total protein concentrations, and inflammatory cytokine levels, together with upregulated α-ENaC and Na+/K+-ATPase α1 expression. Mechanistically, ISM1 promoted α-ENaC and Na+/K+-ATPase α1 expression by suppressing the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway, and these effects were significantly attenuated by GRP78 blockade. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ISM1 promotes alveolar fluid clearance and protects against ALI through a GRP78-dependent mechanism involving inhibition of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, suggesting that ISM1 may have protective effects against ALI.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Chest drainage remains the cornerstone of managing clinically significant pleural disorders and features prominently in both medical and surgical strategies. RECENT FINDINGS: Chest tube drainage technology continues to evolve, offering potential benefits in monitoring, patient mobility, and healthcare utilization. Portable drainage devices and one-way valves may facilitate outpatient management in selected patients, although complications, readmissions, and the need for structured follow-up remain important concerns. Digital drainage systems provide continuous, quantitative air-leak monitoring and may support more objective chest tube removal decisions, reduce chest tube duration, and shorten hospital stays. However, findings from various randomized controlled trials remain inconsistent. The evidence is limited by heterogeneity in patient populations, individual device characteristics, management protocols, and outcome measures. SUMMARY: We aim to provide a practical resource for clinicians to optimize pleural disease management with the different drainage devices available at our disposal. However, individualized device selection and standardized management pathways are essential to improve clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune imprinting, characterized by preferential recall of preexisting vaccine-induced immunity, has been reported following breakthrough infection (BTI) with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants up to XBB. However, whether this phenomenon persists after vaccination with an updated XBB monovalent vaccine lacking the wild-type (WT) antigen and subsequent BTI with the antigenically divergent KP.3 variant remains unclear. METHODS: Convalescent sera were obtained during the KP.3-predominant period in Japan from individuals with KP.3 infection without prior vaccination and from individuals with KP.3 BTI after pre-XBB or XBB mRNA vaccination. Uninfected pre-XBB- and XBB-vaccinated individuals were also included. Strain-specific anti-receptor-binding domain (RBD) IgG titers against WT, BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.3 were measured as surrogate markers of neutralizing activity. Antibody strain specificity was evaluated using variant-to-WT titer ratios. RESULTS: KP.3-specific anti-RBD IgG titers were significantly higher in both vaccinated KP.3-BTI groups than in the unvaccinated KP.3-infection group. The XBB-vaccinated KP.3-BTI group showed an approximately threefold higher geometric mean KP.3-specific titer than the pre-XBB-vaccinated KP.3-BTI group, although the difference was not statistically significant. The same pattern was observed for anti-RBD IgG titers against WT, BA.5, and XBB.1.5. The KP.3/WT ratio was highest in the unvaccinated KP.3-infection group and significantly lower in both vaccinated KP.3-BTI groups. Notably, the ratio in the XBB-vaccinated KP.3-BTI group was comparable to that in uninfected XBB vaccinees. CONCLUSIONS: XBB-vaccinated individuals exhibited numerically higher KP.3-specific antibody responses after KP.3 BTI without preferentially increasing KP.3-specificity, consistent with recall and amplification of cross-reactive memory responses. These findings suggest that immune imprinting-associated recall immunity persists after updated vaccination and may contribute to the immunological benefit of updated vaccination.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by uncontrolled inflammation and high mortality. While mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Exos) show therapeutic potential, their role in regulating macrophage function through PTEN protein stability remains poorly understood. Using LPS-induced mouse ALI and RAW264.7 models, the effects of MSCs or MSC-Exos were evaluated. Inflammatory markers and signaling pathways were analyzed via ELISA, qRT-PCR, Western blot, and immunofluorescence. The underlying molecular mechanism was elucidated using miRNA sequencing, dual-luciferase assays, and ubiquitination analysis. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments using miR-30b-5p mimics and inhibitors were performed in LPS-stimulated macrophages to assess inflammatory cytokine and PTEN expression. Both MSCs and MSC-Exos significantly suppressed TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 expression in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, MSC-Exos upregulated PTEN levels and inhibited PI3K/AKT pathway activation by downregulating the E3 ubiquitin ligase NEDD4L, thereby reducing ubiquitin-mediated PTEN degradation. miR-30b-5p was identified as the key exosomal miRNA directly targeting the 3'UTR of NEDD4L to suppress its expression. miR-30b-5p overexpression mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of MSC-Exos, whereas miR-30b-5p inhibition reversed the suppressive effects of MSC-Exos on TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 expression and attenuated the MSC-Exos-induced increase in PTEN expression in LPS-stimulated macrophages. This study demonstrates that MSC-Exos deliver miR-30b-5p to inhibit NEDD4L, which stabilizes PTEN and suppresses PI3K/AKT activation to alleviate macrophage-driven pulmonary inflammation. These findings reveal a novel mechanism for exosome-mediated immune regulation and indicate that the anti-inflammatory effects of MSC-Exos are dependent on exosomal miR-30b-5p, offering potential therapeutic targets for ALI.

papers.abstract_en: Ion channels and transporters are essential for maintaining pulmonary epithelial homeostasis by regulating ion movement, airway surface liquid composition, and alveolar fluid clearance. Alterations in their expression or function contribute to the pathophysiology of several respiratory diseases. This narrative review summarizes the physiological distribution and functions of major ion channels and transporters in the lung and examines their involvement in four selected conditions representing distinct pathogenic mechanisms: acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS), cystic fibrosis, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and COVID-19. Literature was identified through PubMed searches conducted through September 2026, prioritizing recent mechanistic, experimental, and clinical studies together with landmark publications. In ALI/ARDS, impaired epithelial ion transport contributes to defective alveolar fluid clearance, although clinical trials targeting β-adrenergic stimulation have not demonstrated therapeutic benefit. In cystic fibrosis, CFTR dysfunction disrupts epithelial ion and fluid homeostasis, and CFTR modulators provide an established example of successful mechanism-based therapy. In NSCLC, altered expression and activity of several ion channels are associated with tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and patient outcomes, although most proposed therapeutic applications remain preclinical. In COVID-19, experimental and human tissue studies suggest that SARS-CoV-2 may disrupt epithelial ion transport, but the contribution of individual pathways to pulmonary edema remains incompletely defined. Overall, pulmonary ion channels and transporters represent important links between epithelial physiology and disease, but their translational maturity varies substantially, ranging from clinically validated therapeutic targets to mechanisms that remain hypothesis-generating.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI), a type of inflammatory lung disease. The lack of effective therapeutic interventions makes the search for new agents with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties essential. This study evaluated the prophylactic efficacy of madecassic acid (MSA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid, on experimental mouse model of ALI induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS). The MSA binding affinity to important inflammatory mediators like TLR-4, NF-κB p65 and iNOS was evaluated using in silico docking. Subsequently, male Swiss albino mice administrated MSA (20 mg/kg body weight) as pretreatment for 7 days prior to intranasal LPS challenge (40 mg/kg body weight). Lung morphometry, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) protein content, hematological parameters, oxidative stress, antioxidant enzyme activities, and inflammatory mediators were assessed using biochemical assays, ELISA, qPCR, immunohistochemistry and histopathological examination. Docking analysis demonstrated strong binding interactions between MSA and TLR-4, iNOS and NF-κB p65. The in vivo results showed that pretreatment with MSA significantly reduced pulmonary edema, decreased protein leakage in BALF, and preserved lung histoarchitecture. Furthermore, MSA significantly suppressed neutrophil infiltration, myeloperoxidase activity and decreased the expression of NF-κB p65 protein, iNOS and pro-inflammatory cytokines. In addition, MSA significantly suppressed lipid peroxidation, as indicated by the reduction in MDA level. Collectively, these results suggest that MSA may have the potential to attenuate LPS-induced acute lung injury and may be used as a preventive agent against ALI.
